issue.title: Define staged plan and carry handoff semantics for PR-mode projects

task_type_fields.proposal: Define and implement staged-handoff semantics for PR-mode projects, where `builtin@commit` opens a pull request instead of pushing to the default branch. Epic sase-1pj (plan:202610/staged_handoffs.md, "Non-goals") made every turn-ending command stage its handoff and adopt it only after host finalizers settle; for plan proposals a dirty repository must commit (or file a typed deferral) before the plan gate publishes. In a PR-mode project that commit lands on a PR branch, not on master, so epic phase agents launched after approval start from a base that lacks the lander's or planner's commit. The proposal: decide whether PR-mode plan/epic handoffs should wait for the PR to merge, base successors on the PR branch, or refuse dirty plan proposals with a typed reason, and cover monitor/questions/pipe carry semantics for PR-mode the same way. Proposed by sase-1pj.1 (note #2), carried forward by sase-1pj.1.1.land (note on sase-1pj.1 #4), and triaged by the sase-1pj land agent.
task_type_fields.why_out_of_scope: The approved staged-handoffs plan lists PR-mode projects as an explicit non-goal ("record it as a PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP note"), and sase (this project) runs in direct-push mode, so the epic's acceptance never exercised PR-mode. Defining successor-base semantics for PR-mode is a new capability, not a defect the epic introduced.

issue.creation_reason: sase-1pj.1 proposed this as a follow-up because the staged-handoffs epic explicitly excluded PR-mode projects, whose commit finalizer opens a PR, so successor phase agents cannot see a planner's commit.

payload.description: Epic that introduced staged handoffs and listed PR-mode projects as a non-goal
